finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(), which returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. The OWNER check is never enforced, so any authenticated user can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. They control the `tenant` path parameter and need no OWNER role.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), a destructive wipe of a tenant's data.

trace.note: requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role). The javadoc says it does not throw. The name suggests enforcement but it only returns a boolean.
The boolean result is discarded as a bare statement, so the authorization decision is ignored.
repo.wipe(tenant) runs unconditionally for any user.
By contrast, export() uses the throwing checkRole() at line 32, which confirms the intended pattern.

finding.guards_checked: Checked the enclosing method and the rest of the file. There is no other role check, no throw, and no conditional on the requireRole result. The only authorization on this path is the ignored call. The tenant argument is also not compared with any tenant belonging to the user. User has no tenant field, and roles are global rather than per-tenant, so even a correct OWNER check would not restrict which tenant is wiped. This second issue is noted here, not reported as a separate finding.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole() at src/Admin.java:26 (returns boolean, never throws, result discarded); no other check. The throwing checkRole() is only used in export() at line 32.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls the non-throwing boolean requireRole (defined at :14-16) as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any authenticated caller without the OWNER role.
